title: MAGIC ENGLISH GRADE 5 — WORLD 9: B2 INDEPENDENT & PROFESSIONAL ENGLISH
description: A high-intensity B2 world focused on independent communication, professional and academic-functional English, nuanced discussion, extended comprehension, argumentation, negotiation and confident real-world performance.

targets.active_vocabulary: 2000+ words, collocations, phrasal verbs, idioms, academic-functional terms and professional expressions
targets.reading: 1500–1700 words with inference, synthesis, tone, purpose, evidence and vocabulary-in-context tasks
targets.listening: 13–15 minutes of natural-speed English across interviews, meetings, discussions, announcements and informal conversation
targets.conversation: 18–20 minutes of sustained independent interaction with negotiation, clarification, disagreement and spontaneous follow-up
targets.writing: 380–450 words with advanced cohesion, varied syntax, evidence, counterargument and audience-aware register
targets.real_life: professional communication, academic situations, customer service, travel, public services, digital life, negotiation and problem solving

missions.title: B2 Lexical Expansion — Precision, Register & Word Partnerships
missions.content: Expand active vocabulary beyond common B1 alternatives, distinguish formal and informal choices, build natural word partnerships and use new expressions in extended communication.

missions.title: Grammar Precision Lab — Choose the Meaning You Need
missions.content: Edit and produce complex B2 sentences where grammatical choice changes emphasis, certainty, time reference, quantity, obligation or hypothetical meaning.

missions.title: Advanced Modals & Inference — Read Between the Lines
missions.content: Use evidence to infer what probably happened, what should have happened and what may happen, then explain the reasoning behind each conclusion.

missions.title: Conditional Reasoning — Decisions, Regrets & Consequences
missions.content: Analyze alternative decisions, explain consequences across different time periods and negotiate hypothetical solutions using flexible conditional language.

missions.title: Information Density — Complex Sentences Without Confusion
missions.content: Understand dense B2 sentences, simplify difficult information and then rebuild it into precise, natural language suitable for extended communication.

missions.title: Professional Reporting — Summarize, Attribute & Clarify
missions.content: Summarize meetings, articles and conversations while accurately attributing ideas, separating facts from opinions and maintaining an appropriate professional register.

missions.title: Academic-Functional English — Explain, Compare & Evaluate
missions.content: Explain concepts clearly, compare alternatives, identify causes and effects and evaluate options using precise functional language rather than memorized phrases.

missions.title: Diplomatic Communication — Disagree Without Breaking the Conversation
missions.content: Handle disagreement, correction and criticism diplomatically while asking for clarification, acknowledging another view and keeping communication productive.

missions.title: Information Literacy Mission — Claims, Sources & Evidence
missions.content: Compare information from different texts and spoken sources, identify unsupported claims, recognize degrees of certainty and explain which evidence supports a conclusion.

missions.title: B2 Independent Conversation Lab — Twenty Minutes
missions.content: Maintain a 20-minute conversation across several topics, introduce ideas independently, ask useful follow-up questions and recover naturally when communication breaks down.

missions.title: Reading Mastery — A Real-World Investigation
missions.content: Read an extended investigative-style text, connect information across sections, infer unstated ideas, identify the writer's purpose and support answers with evidence.

missions.title: Listening Mastery — Meetings, Interviews & Everyday Speech
missions.content: Follow a 13–15 minute collection of interviews, meetings and informal conversations, identifying main ideas, specific details, speaker attitudes and implied information.

missions.title: Writing Mastery — Professional Argument & Proposal
missions.content: Write a structured proposal or argumentative text that identifies a problem, evaluates options, supports recommendations and addresses possible objections.

missions.title: Presentation Lab — Present, Defend & Adapt
missions.content: Deliver a structured presentation and respond to unscripted audience questions, adapting explanations and examples when the listener needs clarification.

missions.title: Professional Simulation — Customer, Client & Service Recovery
missions.content: Resolve a complex customer or client problem, explain what went wrong, negotiate alternatives, manage frustration and confirm a practical solution.

missions.title: Academic & Workplace Mission — Meeting, Email & Action Plan
missions.content: Process a realistic workplace or study task from written instructions to discussion, clarification, decision-making and a final professional action-plan message.

missions.title: Negotiation Arena — Priorities, Trade-Offs & Agreement
missions.content: Negotiate a realistic shared decision, explain priorities, make conditional proposals, respond to objections and reach an agreement that both sides can justify.

missions.title: Crisis Communication — Think Clearly When Plans Change
missions.content: Handle a fast-changing scenario involving travel, work, money, appointments and technology. Communicate priorities, revise plans and explain consequences clearly.

missions.title: B2 Independence Marathon — Real Communication Under Pressure
missions.content: Complete a demanding sequence of real-world language tasks with limited preparation, moving from comprehension and editing into spontaneous speaking, professional writing and negotiation.

missions.title: WORLD 9 MASTER QUEST — B2 INDEPENDENT & PROFESSIONAL ENGLISH
missions.content: Final integrated challenge combining advanced vocabulary, grammar precision, extended reading, natural listening, a 20-minute discussion, professional writing, negotiation, presentation and a crisis communication simulation.

quality_rules.progression: World 9 increases independence, professional register, decision-making and spontaneous communication while recycling World 6–8 language.
quality_rules.protected_note: This curriculum file adds Grade 5 World 9 only and does not modify Grade 2, Grade 3 or Grade 4.
